text:
**Short answer:** for most 16-year-olds, the **Starling Teen account** or **Monzo for 16–17s** is the best first account. Both are free, app-based and easy to open on your own.

**Why those two**
- Which? lists both as recommended providers. Starling's Teen account scores 86% and Monzo's 16–17 account scores 85%.
- Finder also ranks Starling first for teens. It names the Starling Teen Bank Account as best for teens.
- Starling includes a Mastercard debit card, works with Apple Pay and Google Pay, and has money tools like "Spaces". Monzo has similar features, including blocked spending on gambling and no overdraft.
- To open Monzo's account you need to be 16 or 17 and UK-based, with photo ID, your own UK mobile number and an email address. Starling says you can apply in minutes with your passport as ID.

**Good alternatives**
- **Nationwide FlexOne** (ages 11–17) is a good choice if you want a building society. It pays 2% AER on balances up to £1,000, and the linked FlexOne Saver pays 5.00% AER (variable) on up to £5,000. Finder rates it best for overseas spending. Check the current rates before you apply, because they change.
- **NatWest Adapt** is useful if you want a high-street bank with interest. If you're 16–17, you can apply for it yourself. It pays 1.60% AER (variable).
- **Barclays, Lloyds, HSBC, Santander and TSB** all have free teen accounts. There isn't much difference between children's bank accounts, so you may want to bank with the same provider as your parents. That can be handy if you want branch access.

**How to choose**
- **Mostly app-based, with budgeting and no fuss:** Starling or Monzo.
- **Branch access or a linked family bank:** NatWest, Lloyds, Barclays or HSBC.
- **Interest on savings:** Nationwide FlexOne with its Saver.
- **Spending abroad:** Starling, Monzo or Nationwide. Barclays charges a 2.99% fee for spending abroad.

**Things to know**
- **Overdrafts:** teen accounts generally don't have them, so you can't go into debt.
- **Protection:** all UK-licensed banks are covered by the FSCS up to £120,000 per person. You don't need to spread your money across banks at this age.
- **Moving later:** most accounts convert to an adult account at 18, and you can switch if you want something different then.

If you tell me what you'll mainly use it for (wages from a job, saving, spending abroad), I can narrow it down to one.
